Jorge Assis, PhD // Nord University, Norway // biodiversityDS, Centre of Marine Sciences, Portugal

Vector data

Importing and ploting vector data

biodiversityDS .

Vector data are composed of vertices - point in space (e.g., longitude and latitude) - that define the shape of the spatial object. The segments that connect vertices determine the type of vector: points, lines and polygons.

Vector point data can be stored in regular text delimited files. When imported to R using the read.table function they are stored as a data.frame object.

# open vector point from text delimited file
distributionRecords <- read.table("../Data/Text delimited/species_presence_records.csv", sep = ";",
    header = TRUE)
# inspect the top records of the data.frame
head(distributionRecords)
Lon Lat
11.080359 42.41853
10.836515 42.31011
15.469765 42.06097
3.297701 42.04394
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .

A data.frame with longitude and latitude records can be mapped directly with the plot function (i.e., xy plot).

# plot distribution records from a data.frame (black points and labels are added)
plot(distributionRecords, main = "Distribution of a marine species", col = "Black", pch = 16,
    ylab = "Latitude", xlab = "Longitude")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .

To transform a data.frame into a spatial object (i.e., vector data) we can use the terra package.

# inspect the class of the object
class(distributionRecords)
## [1] "data.frame"
# load terra package
library(terra)
# transform data.frame into a spatial object
distributionRecords <- vect(distributionRecords, geom = c("Lon", "Lat"))
# inspect the new class of the object
class(distributionRecords)
## [1] "SpatVector"
## attr(,"package")
## [1] "terra"

biodiversityDS .

Vector data are commonly in a ESRI shapefile format. The packages sf and terra deal with shapefiles.

# load terra package
library(terra)
# load a point vector shapefile with terra package
distributionRecords <- vect("../Data/Vector data/Seagrass distribution/cymodocea_nodosa.shp")
# plot point data
plot(distributionRecords, main = "Distribution of a segrass", col = "Black", ylab = "Lat", xlab = "Lon")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .

In R, the attributes of vector data are stored as a data.frame. Each row is a vector element (e.g., point, line, polygon) and each column is an attribute (e.g., date, locality, taxonomy, etc.)

# show attributes of vector data
head(distributionRecords)
year month day country localty kingdom phylum class order family genus
2005 7 NA Greece Eleftheron gulf Plantae Tracheophyta Magnoliopsida Alismatales Cymodoceaceae Cymodocea
2005 7 NA Greece Biamyl Plantae Tracheophyta Magnoliopsida Alismatales Cymodoceaceae Cymodocea
2004 7 NA Greece Nea karvali Plantae Tracheophyta Magnoliopsida Alismatales Cymodoceaceae Cymodocea
2004 7 NA Greece Erateino Plantae Tracheophyta Magnoliopsida Alismatales Cymodoceaceae Cymodocea
2004 7 NA Greece Agiasma Plantae Tracheophyta Magnoliopsida Alismatales Cymodoceaceae Cymodocea
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .

Such like point data, vector line data are commonly stored in a ESRI shapefile format.

# load a line vector shapefile with terra package
coastline <- vect("../Data/Vector data/Coastline/coastline.shp")
# plot spatial line vector
plot(coastline, main = "Global coastline", col = "black", axes = TRUE, ylab = "Latitude", xlab = "Longitude")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .

Vector polygon data are also commonly stored in a ESRI shapefile format.

# load a polygon vector shapefile with terra package
landmass <- vect("../Data/Vector data/Landmass/landmass.shp")
# plot spatial polygon vector with a title
plot(landmass, main = "Global landmass", col = "gray", border = "black", axes = TRUE, ylab = "Latitude",
    xlab = "Longitude")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .

The add=TRUE argument can be used to overlay multiple vectors in a plot use .

plot(landmass, main = "Distribution of a segrass species", col = "Gray", border = "Gray", axes = TRUE,
    ylab = "Latitude", xlab = "Longitude")
plot(distributionRecords, col = "Black", pch = 20, size = 0.25, add = TRUE)

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

Conversion between spatial object formats

biodiversityDS .

Some operations (i.e., functions) are only available for a specific format (i.e., sf or terra). Spatial objects can be converted between formats.

# load a polygon vector shapefile with terra package and inspect its class
landmass <- vect("../Data/Vector data/Landmass/landmass.shp")
class(landmass)
## [1] "SpatVector"
## attr(,"package")
## [1] "terra"
# load sf package
library(sf)
# convert terra object to sf object and inspect its class
landmass <- st_as_sf(landmass)
class(landmass)
## [1] "sf"         "data.frame"
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .
# load a polygon vector shapefile with sf package and inspect its class
landmass <- st_read("../Data/Vector data/Landmass/landmass.shp", quiet = TRUE)
class(landmass)
## [1] "sf"         "data.frame"
# convert sf object to terra object and inspect its class
landmass <- vect(landmass)
class(landmass)
## [1] "SpatVector"
## attr(,"package")
## [1] "terra"
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

Generate vector data in R

biodiversityDS .

To generate (i.e., to draw) vector data in R we can use the drawFeatures function from package mapedit.
To give geographic context, a global map can be added with the leaflet package.

# Load necessary libraries
library(leaflet)
library(mapedit)

# create a base leaflet map
baseMap <- leaflet()
baseMap <- addTiles(baseMap)

# drawing vector polygon in the Viewer pane
drawnFeatures <- drawFeatures(baseMap)
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .


In the Viewer pane a tool is shown to generate vector data. The tool will generate an sf object.

# navigate the map and use the polygon tool to a draw vector; click to create vertices,
# click first point or click 'finish' to close the polygon; click 'Done' button in the map
# interface when done drawing all features; type 'Esc' to quit the tool at any time.
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

Exporting vector data

biodiversityDS .

Spatial data can be exported to multiple GIS standard formats, such as ESRI shapefile or GeoPackage.

ESRI shapefile, a format with distinct files storing geographic location and associated attribute information.

# export vector data to shapefile
writeVector(x = landmass, filename = "directory/output_name.shp", filetype = "ESRI Shapefile",
    overwrite = TRUE)

GeoPackage, defined by a unique spatial database file.

# export vector data to GeoPackage
writeVector(x = landmass, filename = "directory/output_name.gpkg", filetype = "GPKG", overwrite = TRUE)
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .

Vector data operations

biodiversityDS .

Operations that change the geometry of spatial objects.

Crop vector data to a different extent

# read landmass from an R package
landmass <- vect("../Data/Vector data/Landmass/landmass.shp")

# generate an extent object (region of interest, order: xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
mediterraneanExtent <- ext(-15, 45, 30, 47.5)
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .
# for inspection, plot the landmass and the extent region
plot(landmass, main = "Global landmass", col = "gray", border = "gray", axes = TRUE)
plot(mediterraneanExtent, border = "black", add = TRUE)
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .
# generate a new polygon based on the provided extent
mediterraneanLandmass <- crop(landmass, mediterraneanExtent)
# plot the new polygon
plot(mediterraneanLandmass, main = "Mediterranean Sea", col = "gray", border = "gray", axes = TRUE,
    ylab = "Latitude", xlab = "Longitude")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

Raster data

Raster data

biodiversityDS .

Raster data uses a regular grid to represent a spatial gradient. The terra package deals with raster data.

# load libraries
library(terra)
# Open a raster layer with the global sea surface temperature
seaSurfaceTemp <- rast("../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif")
# inspect the raster object
seaSurfaceTemp
## class       : SpatRaster 
## dimensions  : 3600, 7200, 1  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
## resolution  : 0.05, 0.05  (x, y)
## extent      : -180, 180, -90, 90  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
## coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) 
## source      : Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif 
## name        : Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax 
## min value   :                              -1.846673 
## max value   :                              34.883312
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

Plotting raster data

biodiversityDS .
# Plot a raster layer
plot(seaSurfaceTemp, main = "Global maximum sea surface temperature")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

Combining different rasters

biodiversityDS .

Combining different raster layers into a unique object. These must have the same extent and resolution.

# Open a raster layer with the global sea surface temperature
seaSurfaceTemp <- rast("../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif")
# Open a raster layer with the global bottom surface temperature
seaBottomTemp <- rast("../Data/Raster data/Present Benthic OceanTemperature LtMax.tif")
# combine the raster layers
seaTemp <- c(seaSurfaceTemp, seaBottomTemp)
# Plot the raster layers
plot(seaTemp, axes = TRUE, main = "Global maximum sea temperatures")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .

Combining different raster layers into a unique object, directly from file vector.

# create a vector with the path to the raster layers
file1 <- "../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif"
file2 <- "../Data/Raster data/Present Benthic OceanTemperature LtMax.tif"
myFiles <- c(file1, file2)
# combine the raster layers
seaTemp <- rast(myFiles)
# plot the raster layers
plot(seaTemp)
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

Subsetting combined raster data

biodiversityDS .

To subset combined raster layers use the subset function or work with indices.

# create a vector with the path to the raster layers
myFiles <- c("../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif", "../Data/Raster data/Present Benthic OceanTemperature LtMax.tif",
    "../Data/Raster data/Present Surface Nitrate Mean.tif", "../Data/Raster data/Bathymetry.tif")
# combining the raster layers
environmentLayers <- rast(myFiles)
# inspect the combined raster layers raster layers
names(environmentLayers)
## [1] "Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax"
## [2] "Present Benthic OceanTemperature LtMax"
## [3] "Present Surface Nitrate Mean"          
## [4] "Bathymetry"
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

Subsetting combined raster data

biodiversityDS .

To subset combined raster layers use the subset or work with indices.

# subset the combined raster layers
environmentLayersSubset <- subset(environmentLayers, c(1, 3))
# inspect the combined raster layers
names(environmentLayersSubset)
## [1] "Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax"
## [2] "Present Surface Nitrate Mean"
# subset the combined raster layers (note the double brackets)
environmentLayersSubset <- environmentLayers[[c(1, 3)]]
# inspect the combined raster layers
names(environmentLayersSubset)
## [1] "Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax"
## [2] "Present Surface Nitrate Mean"
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

Renaming raster data

biodiversityDS .

For simplicity, raster layers can be renamed.

# inspect the combined raster layers raster layers
names(environmentLayers)
## [1] "Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax"
## [2] "Present Benthic OceanTemperature LtMax"
## [3] "Present Surface Nitrate Mean"          
## [4] "Bathymetry"
# rename the combined raster layers
names(environmentLayers) <- c("Temperature Max", "Temperature Min", "Nitrate", "Bathymetry")
# inspect the combined raster layers
names(environmentLayers)
## [1] "Temperature Max" "Temperature Min" "Nitrate"         "Bathymetry"

Raster data operations

biodiversityDS .

Crop raster data

# load the raster layer
seaSurfaceTemp <- rast("../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif")

# define the extent to crop (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
mediterraneanExtent <- ext(-15, 45, 30, 47.5)
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .
# for inspection, plot the raster layer and the extent region
plot(seaSurfaceTemp, main = "Global sea surface temperatures")
plot(mediterraneanExtent, add = TRUE)

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .
# crop with polygon (region)
mediterraneanSeaSurfaceTemp <- crop(seaSurfaceTemp, mediterraneanExtent)
# plot sst of the region of interest
plot(mediterraneanSeaSurfaceTemp, main = "Mediterranean sea surface temperature")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .

Mask raster data

# load a raster mask
coastalRegion <- rast("../Data/Raster data/CoastLine.tif")
# plot the raster mask
plot(coastalRegion, col = "black")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .
# load the raster layer
seaSurfaceTemp <- rast("../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif")
# mask with raster layer
coastalSeaSurfaceTemp <- mask(seaSurfaceTemp, coastalRegion)
# plot the masked layer
plot(coastalSeaSurfaceTemp, main = "Coastal sea surface temperature")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .

Combine different rasters by resampling

# load raster layers
landCover <- rast("../Data/Raster data/LandCover GLCNMO.tif")
airTemperature <- rast("../Data/Raster data/AirTemperature Surface Ltmax.tif")
# inspect resolution
res(landCover)
## [1] 0.004166667 0.004166667
# inspect resolution
res(airTemperature)
## [1] 0.05 0.05
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .
# resample to layer to match extent and resolution
landCover <- resample(landCover, airTemperature, method = "mode")

# combine layers into one object
myLayers <- c(landCover, airTemperature)

myLayers
## class       : SpatRaster 
## dimensions  : 3600, 7200, 2  (nrow, ncol, nlyr)
## resolution  : 0.05, 0.05  (x, y)
## extent      : -180, 180, -90, 90  (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)
## coord. ref. : lon/lat WGS 84 (EPSG:4326) 
## sources     : memory  
##               AirTemperature Surface Ltmax.tif  
## varnames    : AirTemperature Surface Ltmax 
##               AirTemperature Surface Ltmax 
## names       : LandCover GLCNMO, AirTemperature Surface Ltmax 
## min values  :                1,                     -8.32791 
## max values  :               20,                     40.04485

Algebra in raster data

biodiversityDS .

Change the values of a raster layer

# Change the values of a raster layer by summing a constant value
seaSurfaceTemp <- rast("../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif")
seaSurfaceTempKelvin <- seaSurfaceTemp + 273.15
plot(seaSurfaceTempKelvin, main = "Maximum sea surface temperatures (Kelvin)")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .

Use algebra functions between raster layers

# open two temperature layers of the minimum and maximum extremes
seaSurfaceTempMax <- rast("../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif")
seaSurfaceTempMin <- rast("../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMin.tif")
# determine the range of temperatures by simple a simple operation between layers
rangeSeaSurfaceTemp <- seaSurfaceTempMax - seaSurfaceTempMin
plot(rangeSeaSurfaceTemp, main = "Range of sea surface temperatures")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .

Use algebra functions between raster layers

# combine two raster layers and determine their mean
myFiles <- c("../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif", "../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMin.tif")
seaSurfaceTemp <- rast(myFiles)
# determine the average temperature between layers using the app function
averageSeaSurfaceTemp <- app(seaSurfaceTemp, fun = mean)
plot(averageSeaSurfaceTemp, main = "Average sea surface temperature")

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

Classify (or reclassify) raster values

biodiversityDS .

The classify function reclassifies raster values based on the argument rcl, a three-column matrix “from-to-becomes”

# open a raster layer
temperatureLayer <- rast("../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif")
# from-to-becomes matrix
rclmat <- data.frame(from = c(-Inf, 12, 25), to = c(12, 25, Inf), becomes = c(0, 1, 0))
temperatureLayerReclass <- classify(temperatureLayer, rclmat)
plot(temperatureLayerReclass)

Correlation between predictors

biodiversityDS .

Correlation between predictors is important to avoid multicollinearity. The getCorrPlot function from the biodiversityDS package can be used to calculate and plot the correlation between raster layers.

# create a vector with the path to the raster layers 
myFiles <- c("../Data/Raster data/Present Surface OceanTemperature LtMax.tif", # Max. surface temperature
             "../Data/Raster data/Present Benthic OceanTemperature LtMax.tif", # Max. benthic temperature
             "../Data/Raster data/Present Surface Nitrate Mean.tif", # Nitrate
             "../Data/Raster data/Bathymetry.tif" # Bathymetry
             )
# combining the raster layers
environmentLayers <- rast(myFiles)
# change name of layers for simplicity
names(environmentLayers) <- c("Surface temperature","Benthic temperature","Nitrate","Bathymetry")
S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .
# get correlation between pairs of layers
correlations <- getCorrPlot(environmentLayers)

S2 // R as a Geographic Information System

biodiversityDS .
